form: ((discriminator & 0x7FF) << 20) | ((manager slot & 0xF) << 16) | record index
range: discriminator 1 to 2047; manager selector 0 to 4; index below the slot's +0x20 and the pool's count
invalid: 0; a selector of 5 or more; a discriminator that no longer matches the actor's +0x16
resolved_by: 0x003588B0(handle) returns the actor or null
reuse: 0x002659D0 advances the record's discriminator ((old + 1) & 0x7FF, 0 replaced by 1), so a handle taken before stops resolving

form: the battle unit of an actor, reached from an actor handle
range: a resolving actor handle whose actor has a unit
invalid: any handle while 0x02089340 bit 4 is clear
resolved_by: 0x0031B7E0(handle) returns the actor's unit +0x30 when 0x02089340 bit 4 is set; 0x0031B760(actor) is the null-guarded form
reuse: as the actor handle

form: (dword [entry + 0x24] << 16) | word [entry + 0x1A] | 0x8000: the entry's stamp, its slot and bit 15
range: slot 0 to 0x7F of the 128 entries at 0x0215FDA0
invalid: 0; bit 15 clear; a slot of 0x80 or more; a stamp that no longer matches
resolved_by: 0x002E97C0(handle) returns the entry when its recomputed handle equals the argument, else null
reuse: an entry's handle stops working the moment the entry is retired; a script must re-resolve

form: letter class in bits 16-23, number in bits 0-15
range: the eleven letter classes the model asset list names (c0 is 0x00630000)
invalid: class M, which maps to kind 0x12 with no path array
resolved_by: the letter class gives the resource kind and the number the index (the class table of the model asset list)
reuse: fixed: an id always names the same model

form: a resource kind and an id within it
range: kind 0 to 40, id 0 to 4,999
invalid: a size of -1 in the file-size table (no file for that pair)
resolved_by: 0x002DF980(kind, id) gives the path, 0x002DF960(kind, id) the size at 0x02EC3EE0 + 4 x (kind x 5000 + id)
reuse: fixed for a language: the path arrays and the table are set once at boot

form: the address of a 16-byte slot in an arena's slot table, with tag bits in its low two bits
range: tagged and at least 0x100000
invalid: an untagged value, a value below 0x100000, or a slot whose check word +0x06 differs
resolved_by: 0x0036A000(handle) (0x003AB880 passes an untagged value through)
reuse: a freed slot returns to the arena's free chain; the check word tells a stale handle apart

form: slot in bits 0-5, a 22-bit counter (0x02EBDBB0) in bits 6-27, 3 in bits 28-31
range: slots 0 to 31
invalid: 0 (no free ticket: 0x003B38B0 returns 0 with no context)
resolved_by: the record at 0x02EBCD80 + slot x 0x38, found by the low six bits
reuse: a recycled slot gets a new id from the counter

form: serial << 8 | slot
range: slots of the trail pool; the serial wraps to 1 above 0xFFFFFF
invalid: 0 (a free entry, or no entry free); 0xFFFF in the record's handle fields
resolved_by: every pool routine compares the handle with the entry's own +0
reuse: a freed entry takes a new serial, so a stale handle is harmless

form: serial << 8 | slot
range: the 128 slots of the registry at 0x02ADBFE0, 0x20 bytes a slot
invalid: a handle not in the live list
resolved_by: 0x00377360(handle) finds it in the registry's live list
reuse: the release frees the slot

form: generation x 256 + slot + 1
range: the vibration slots
invalid: a stale generation: every handle function compares it first, and 0x0035B240 returns 0
reuse: 0x0035B1A0 raises the slot's generation when it frees it

form: the element's address, kept in a dword (0x00319E05)
range: the 13 pickup elements
invalid: 0 when all 13 are in use; 0x003FA730 reads [handle + 0x272] before any null test
resolved_by: the address itself
reuse: an element is free again once its +0x272 bit 0 is clear; with all 13 in use 0x003FA160 returns 0 and no pickup is made (the state +0x04 and the oldest-pickup eviction belong to the ten-slot pickup pool)

form: a 32-bit offset from the 64-bit base at 0x01F83530, which is 0 in this build: a pointer's low 32 bits
range: addresses below 4 GB
invalid: none of its own; a pointer above 4 GB loses its high half
resolved_by: 0x0020E600(u) zero-extends and adds the base back
reuse: as the pointer it encodes

form: class nibble id >> 12 (0 to 0xE) and index id & 0xFFF
range: nibbles 0 to 0xE; the index below the class's count
invalid: 0xFFFF (none); nibble 0xF (0x00309440 returns -1); 0x1000, the Unarmed row, which 0x003008A0 refuses
made_by: the tables and scripts that name items and abilities
resolved_by: 0x00309440(id) gives the class (nibble + 5); 0x003008A0 changes what the party owns
reuse: fixed: an id always names the same row

form: a battle action id, or an internal order
range: actions 0 to 0x21E (with a target list); orders 0x4000 to 0x4166 (no target list)
invalid: any other id: the commit returns 0 (0x0030F7D9-0x0030F7EC)
made_by: the gambits, menus and enemy order sets
resolved_by: the commit 0x0030F760; the action table 0x02EBF138 for an action
reuse: fixed

form: one integer per map: mapjump's first argument, save payload +0x1044
range: the field ids of the three per-map tables
invalid: an id with no row in the tables
resolved_by: the archive file table, MapRef (8 bytes per field id, 0x00264F90) and the music table 0x003EAA70
reuse: fixed: stable across languages

form: group x 1000 + row, or a row's own id under group x 10000
range: groups 0 to 27; the row below the table's +0x04
invalid: a group of 28 or more, a file not resident, a row past the table: the empty string 0x01CEB638; a negative id passes the group test (< 28) and is not refused
resolved_by: 0x002F9860(id) (group x 1000 + row); 0x002F9920(id) (a linear search under group x 10000)
reuse: fixed per language file

form: bank in bits 11-15, row in bits 0-10
range: 15 banks; rows below each bank's count
invalid: a bank or row past its count: 0x003214B0 returns 0
made_by: the battle tables that name words
resolved_by: 0x003214B0(word); many readers index the banks inline with no bounds test
reuse: fixed

form: sheet x 64 + page
invalid: 512 to 0x7FFF: no container, the row shows what the atlas last held
resolved_by: 0x00292390 through the sheet slots
reuse: fixed

form: an entry number of a script's text section
range: below the first dword / 4 (sign-extended, shifted right by 2: 0x00264D74-0x00264D7D); the id masked to 24 bits
invalid: an id at or above the count: the empty string 0x01CEB638
resolved_by: 0x00264D60 (section 2), 0x00264D90 (section 3)
reuse: fixed per script image

form: a seat of one of the five slot maps in the battle state block [0x02EBF190] (+0x5A48, +0x5A5A, +0x5A6C, +0x5A7E, +0x5A90), two bytes each
range: seats 0 to 8: 0-3 the active members, 4-8 the reserve; maps 0 to 4
invalid: a seat whose low byte is 0xFF is empty
made_by: joining, leaving and the scenes that fix the party
resolved_by: 0x0031B9F0(seat, map) returns the seat's low byte, the member selector
reuse: a seat is rewritten whenever the party changes

form: the low byte of a party seat
range: the rows of the party table and of the forty member records; the leader's at +0x5AA4
invalid: 0xFF (an empty seat)
resolved_by: the party table and the member records by row
reuse: fixed: a selector always names the same member

form: one of the twelve derived inventory lists the menus page through
range: 0 to 11; each list's entry count is at save +0x47B8 + 4 x list
invalid: an empty entry holds the id 0xFFFF
made_by: 0x00252E60 appends an id when its count goes from 0 to non-zero, through 0x00325F40's maps of the class nibble (and an equipment row's category byte) to a list
resolved_by: 0x00252F40(list), which the Inventory's categories and the shop tabs read
reuse: the clear-all 0x003047F0 and 0x00253480 empty all twelve (0x00253240(i, 1))

form: serial << 8 | slot, kept at the record's +0x00
range: slots 0 to 63 of the 0x60-byte records at [0x02B404E0]; the serial 1 to 0xFFFFFF
invalid: 0, which marks a free record and is what 0x003B4160 returns with none free; a handle that no longer equals the record's +0x00
made_by: 0x003B4160 takes the first record whose +0x00 is 0
resolved_by: 0x003B4770(handle) returns the record's +0x20 part only when its +0x00 equals the handle, else null
reuse: each new record takes the next serial (0x02B404C4, wrapping to 1 above 0xFFFFFF), so a stale handle stops matching

form: generation << 8 | slot, kept at the command slot's +0x10
range: slots 0 to 159 of the 0xE0-byte slots at [0x02B40528]; the generation 1 to 0xFFFFFF
invalid: 0 with no free slot (0x003B56D0); -1 in a presentation entry's +0x35C means none; a handle that no longer equals the slot's +0x10
made_by: 0x003B56D0 takes the first slot whose +0x40 bit 0 is clear
resolved_by: the channel setters find the slot [0x02B40528] + (handle & 0xFF) x 0xE0 and write nothing when its +0x10 is not the handle
reuse: each start takes the next generation (0x02B40520, wrapping to 1 above 0xFFFFFF; 0x003B6890 resets it to 0), so a stale handle stops matching

form: serial << 8 | index, kept at the entry's +0x50 (0x003AEDE0)
range: index 0 to 127 of the pool 0x02B3F530; the serial 0x02B3F538 wraps past 0xFFFFFF to 1
invalid: 0 (no inactive entry)
resolved_by: nothing: no instruction resolves the handle or compares it with an entry; every reader reaches the entries through the list links at record +0x550
reuse: nothing looks a handle up, so a stale one is harmless
